scope: Unchanged source blocks. Complete setup includes monitor restoration lines 76-79 with fixture-supplied saved position; partial controls remain useful for focused tests. No game loop or pulse catcher is executed.

defaults.source:
window_width = CharSettings['window_width'] || 120
window_height = CharSettings['window_height'] || 25
window_position = CharSettings['window_position']
window_decorated = CharSettings['window_decorated']

locals.source:
bar = label = overlay = normal_bar_style = bar_style = window = done = window_close = nil

# GC anchor: ruby-gnome2's signal_connect stores the handler Proc only in a
# C-side GLib::Closure that Ruby's GC cannot see. Without a Ruby-side reference,
# the block becomes collectable and, after a GC pass (often during a long idle
# period), GTK invokes a freed object -> "method 'call' called on terminated
# object", killing Gtk.main and freezing Lich. Anchoring every handler here for
# the script's lifetime prevents that. (Same fix map.lic already uses.)
_prevent_gc = []

setup.source:
Gtk.queue {
	window = Gtk::Window.new
	window.title = "#{Char.name} Mana Timer"
	delete_handler = proc { window_close = true }
	_prevent_gc << delete_handler
	window.signal_connect('delete_event', &delete_handler)
	bar = Gtk::ProgressBar.new
	# This GTK3 build stacks a ProgressBar's own text *above* the trough, so we
	# hide it and overlay a label on top of the bar instead.
	bar.show_text = false
	bar.height_request = 18
	bar.width_request = 20
	label = Gtk::Label.new
	label.halign = Gtk::Align::CENTER
	label.valign = Gtk::Align::CENTER
	overlay = Gtk::Overlay.new
	overlay.add(bar)
	overlay.add_overlay(label)
	overlay.set_overlay_pass_through(label, true)
	bar.add_events(Gdk::Event::BUTTON_PRESS_MASK)
	press_handler = proc { |owner, ev| Gtk.queue { window.decorated = !window.decorated? if ev.button == 3 } }
	_prevent_gc << press_handler
	bar.signal_connect('button_press_event', &press_handler)
	window.add(overlay)
	window.show_all
	window.decorated = window_decorated unless window_decorated.nil?
	window.resize(window_width.to_i, window_height.to_i)
	_geometry = Gdk::Display.default.default_screen.get_monitor_geometry(Gdk::Display.default.default_screen.get_monitor_at_point(window_position[0].to_i, window_position[1].to_i))
	window_position[0] = [[0, window_position[0].to_i].max, (_geometry.width-window_width.to_i)].min
	window_position[1] = [[0, window_position[1].to_i].max, (_geometry.height-window_height.to_i)].min
	window.move(window_position[0].to_i, window_position[1].to_i)
	window.set_keep_above(true)
  	
  	# GTK3: style via a CSS provider on the bar's style context.
  	css_provider = Gtk::CssProvider.new
  	bar.style_context.add_provider(css_provider, Gtk::StyleProvider::PRIORITY_APPLICATION)
  	# min-height + padding:0 keep the trough/fill from being squashed by GTK3 theme defaults.
  	_bar_base = "progressbar { padding: 0; min-height: 18px; } progressbar trough { min-height: 18px; padding: 0; border-width: 0; } progressbar progress { background-image: none; min-height: 18px; "
  	normal_bar_style = proc { css_provider.load_from_data("#{_bar_base} background-color: #06b025; }") }
  	bar_style = proc { css_provider.load_from_data("#{_bar_base} background-color: #b02506; }") }
  	bar_style.call

  	# Keep the overlaid label legible on top of the colored fill.
  	label_css = Gtk::CssProvider.new
  	label_css.load_from_data("label { color: #000000; font-weight: bold; padding: 0; margin: 0; min-height: 0; }")
  	label.style_context.add_provider(label_css, Gtk::StyleProvider::PRIORITY_APPLICATION)

	done = true
}

tick.source:
Gtk.queue {
		bar.fraction = ticks / 120.0 % 1
		label.text =  "#{ "%02d" %(ticks/60)}:#{ "%02d" % (ticks%60)}"
		if ticks == 76 || ticks == 16
			bar_style.call
		end
	}
